name: Northern Wei Buddha Face
description: This is a fragmentary clay sculpture of a Buddha's face from the Northern Wei Dynasty. The piece is missing the eyes, forehead, and parts of the cheeks, yet the remaining features are remarkably serene.

name: Eastern Han Gilt Feather Man
description: This gilded bronze figurine depicts a feathered immortal, a common motif in Han Dynasty mythology. The figure has pointed ears, wings, and holds a decorated rectangular vessel.

name: Roman Glass Bottle
description: This is a blown glass bottle from the Eastern Han Dynasty, imported from the Roman Empire. It features swirling white and colored threads against a dark background.

name: Han Dynasty Dancer Figurine
description: This is a painted pottery figurine of a female dancer from the Han Dynasty, likely depicting a performer of the 'Seven-Plate Dance'. She strikes a dynamic pose with flowing sleeves.

name: Warring States Gold-Silver Ding
description: The vessel's surface is adorned with symmetrical floral and geometric patterns. The lost-wax casting and inlay techniques demonstrate the peak of bronze craftsmanship in ancient China.
